definitions: O is the spherical mirror's curvature center, called its 光心 in the original, not a thin lens optical center.
The principal axis passes through O and the mirror vertex P; secondary axes pass through O.
Point focusing and focal-plane construction retain small ray-height and small-angle paraxial conditions.
A small-angle secondary-axis parallel bundle approximately focuses at the focal plane; this is not an exact arbitrary off-axis or wide-aperture claim.
A ray through the principal focus reflects approximately parallel to the principal axis in the same paraxial model.

claims.claim: Given an object's position relative to a spherical mirror, geometrical construction locates its image; construct the image of individual object points.
claims.requiredScope: Image construction, not an invented numerical image solution.

claims.claim: A straightedge-and-compass construction of a point image also explains the direction of an arbitrary reflected ray.
claims.requiredScope: Keep the construction purpose; do not replace the lesson with mirror-equation calculations.

claims.claim: For incident ray AC, construct a secondary axis parallel to AC. D is its intersection with the focal plane; reflected line CD passes through D.
claims.requiredScope: The secondary axis passes through O by the accepted axis definition. D is not the principal focus or the intersection of AC with the focal plane. Keep the paraxial construction restriction.

claims.claim: A bundle parallel to a secondary axis reflects toward one point of the focal plane in the approximation already established.
claims.requiredScope: Replace the backwards figure-144 dependency with a self-contained explanation, not an invented figure-144 visual PASS. Do not claim exact focusing of all aperture sizes or angles.

claims.claim: One ray along the secondary axis and through O identifies D: reflection remains on that line, so D is on both the axis and focal plane.
claims.requiredScope: O means curvature center. Reflection at the spherical surface is not thin-lens nondeviation at O. The axis in this argument is the secondary axis parallel to AC.

claims.claim: Four convenient ray constructions determine the image of an object point A.
claims.requiredScope: Preserve all four distinct named ray families and the A/A1 point-image task.

claims.claim: AOC goes through the mirror's curvature center O; COA retraces the same straight line after reflection.
claims.requiredScope: Preserve AOC/COA and the reason involving the spherical-surface normal; do not substitute mirror vertex P for O.

claims.claim: AFK passes through principal focus F before meeting the mirror at K; its reflected ray is parallel to the principal axis.
claims.requiredScope: Preserve AFK, F, K and the paraxial restriction.

claims.claim: AP reaches the mirror vertex P; incident and reflected rays are symmetric about the principal axis.
claims.requiredScope: P is the vertex, and the principal axis supplies the normal at P; angles are measured from the normal.

claims.claim: AE is parallel to the principal axis; reflected EFA1 passes through the principal focus F.
claims.requiredScope: Preserve AE/EFA1 and do not omit F or silently change the meaning of A1. Keep the paraxial restriction.

claims.claim: The reflected rays pass through A's image point A1 in the construction; any two of the listed rays suffice.
claims.requiredScope: A usable pair must determine an intersection rather than be the same drawn line. Qualifying common-point convergence as paraxial is a scientific clarification, not literal source wording.

claims.claim: Other rays striking reflective parts also pass through A1 within the image-construction approximation; individual special rays may be absent.
claims.requiredScope: Do not turn an unavailable ray into a reflected one or claim a nonexistent reflective surface.

claims.claim: The medical concave mirror example has a small central hole, so no ray reflects from that missing central surface; rays from remaining mirror surface form the image.
claims.requiredScope: Retain the medical example and central-hole mechanism. Do not add aperture dimensions, an unsupported apparatus function or a numerical image result.

claims.claim: Constructing images of the object's edge points is sufficient to construct the object's image.
claims.requiredScope: Preserve the 边缘 emphasis and edge-point identity; do not generalize this into exactly two arbitrary object points for every shape.

nonTextBlocks.textReviewScope: Identity and association only; no pixel or figure verdict.
Identity and association only; no pixel or figure verdict.

questions.scope: Ask the law of reflection; the scientific meaning includes coplanar incident ray, reflected ray and normal, with equal incidence/reflection angles measured from the normal. Do not add a separate numerical problem or replace this identity.

questions.literal: **2.** 什么是球面镜的主焦点？
questions.scope: Ask the principal-focus definition for a spherical mirror. Accepted n70 context distinguishes concave actual rays from convex backward extensions and retains paraxial focusing. Do not silently require an exact all-ray focus.

questions.literal: **3.** 为作出球面镜所成的像，取什么光线为宜？
questions.scope: Ask which convenient rays to use for image construction, preserving the lesson's four-ray identity. Do not replace it with object/image-distance computation.
